test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 17 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution is related with protection in respect of conviction for offences?
solution:
The correct answer is__** 20.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Article 20**-No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the **same offence repeatedly.**
 
• No person accused of any offence shall be forced to be an** observer against himself.**
 
• No person shall be convicted of **any offence except for contravention** of the law in force at the time of the commission of the act **imposed as an offence, nor be subjected to a penalty** greater than that which might have been inflicted under the law in force at the time of the commission of the offence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 18(1)** **abolishes all titles**. It forbids the State to confer titles on anybody whether a citizen or a non-citizen. Military and academic distinctions are, but, exempted from the prohibition.
 
• ​**The Right to Protection of Life and personal liberty** is the important object of **Article 21 **and it is a right guaranteed as opposed to State Action as eminent from violation of such right by private individuals.
 
• Everyone has the **right to freedom of opinion under Article 19.**
